title: Solomon Builds the Temple
summary: At Gibeon Solomon offers a thousand burnt offerings, and God offers him whatever he asks; he asks for wisdom and receives wealth and honor too. He sends to Huram of Tyre for cedar, fir and craftsmen and builds the temple on Mount Moriah, and the ark is brought in. When the priests come out, the glory of the LORD fills the house. Solomon prays at its dedication, fire comes down from heaven, and the LORD appears again, promising to hear if his people humble themselves.

title: Solomon's Reign and the Queen of Sheba
summary: Solomon builds cities, fortifies others, and sets the priests and Levites in their courses, with burnt offerings on the Sabbaths and feasts. His fleet brings gold from Ophir. The queen of Sheba tests him with hard questions, is amazed at his wisdom and house, and gives him spices and gold. His yearly income is 666 talents of gold, and his throne is ivory overlaid with gold. Solomon reigns forty years and is buried in the city of David.

title: Rehoboam and the Division
summary: Rehoboam answers the people harshly at Shechem and ten tribes leave him. When he gathers an army to fight them, the prophet Shemaiah tells him to stop, and Rehoboam fortifies cities in Judah; priests and Levites from the north come to him. After he abandons the law, Shishak of Egypt invades with 1,200 chariots and takes the temple treasures. Shemaiah says they have forsaken God; the leaders humble themselves, and God spares the city from destruction. Rehoboam reigns seventeen years.

title: Abijah and Asa
summary: Abijah of Judah speaks to Jeroboam from Mount Zemaraim, and God gives Judah victory, with 500,000 of Israel killed. Asa then removes foreign altars and builds fortresses, and when Zerah the Ethiopian comes with a huge army, he cries to the LORD and wins. At the prophet Azariah's urging the people renew the covenant. Late in life Asa pays Ben-hadad of Syria with temple silver, imprisons the seer Hanani who rebukes him, and in his disease seeks only physicians.

title: Jehoshaphat
summary: Jehoshaphat strengthens Judah, sends officials and Levites to teach the book of the law, and receives tribute. He allies with Ahab by marriage and joins him at Ramoth-gilead, and the seer Jehu rebukes him afterward. He appoints judges and tells them to judge in fear of the LORD. When Moab, Ammon and men of Mount Seir attack, Jehoshaphat proclaims a fast and prays; Jahaziel says the battle is God's, singers go before the army, and the enemies destroy each other. His joint fleet is wrecked.

title: Jehoram, Ahaziah, Athaliah and Joash
summary: Jehoram of Judah kills his brothers and marries Ahab's daughter, and Elijah writes to him that disease will kill him. After Jehoram and Ahaziah die, Athaliah kills the royal seed except Joash, hidden by his aunt Jehoshabeath, and is put to death when the priest Jehoiada crowns Joash. Joash repairs the temple with a collection chest, but after Jehoiada dies he listens to the princes, turns to idols, and has Jehoiada's son Zechariah stoned. The Syrians invade, and Joash is murdered.

title: Amaziah, Uzziah and Jotham
summary: Amaziah hires Israelite troops, sends them home on a prophet's word, defeats Edom, then brings back Edom's gods and worships them. He challenges Joash of Israel, loses, and Jerusalem's wall is broken. Uzziah rules well while he seeks God, defeats the Philistines, builds towers and has a large army, but grows proud, enters the temple to burn incense, and is struck with leprosy on his forehead as the priests oppose him; he lives apart. Jotham rules faithfully and grows mighty.

title: Ahaz and Hezekiah's Reforms
summary: Ahaz of Judah worships Baal, burns his children, and is defeated by Syria and Israel, though the prophet Oded gets Israel to return its captives. Ahaz seeks help from Assyria, shuts the temple doors, and sacrifices to Damascus's gods. Hezekiah, in his first year, reopens and cleanses the temple, and the Levites sing and burn sacrifices. He invites all Israel to a Passover in the second month, and many come and keep it with joy. The people then destroy idols and bring tithes.

title: Sennacherib's Invasion and Hezekiah's Pride
summary: After Hezekiah's acts of faithfulness, Sennacherib of Assyria invades Judah. Hezekiah stops the springs outside the city, repairs the wall, and tells the people that there is a greater power with them. Sennacherib's servants mock the LORD, and Hezekiah and Isaiah cry to heaven; the LORD sends an angel who cuts off the Assyrian warriors, and Sennacherib returns in shame. Hezekiah falls ill and grows proud, humbles himself, and prospers; he also channels the Gihon spring's water into the city.

title: Manasseh's Repentance and Josiah's Reforms
summary: Manasseh does great evil, building altars for the host of heaven in the temple; the Assyrians take him in chains to Babylon, where he humbles himself and God restores him, and he then removes the idols. His son Amon is killed. Josiah, seeking God from the age of sixteen, purges Judah, repairs the temple, and finds the book of the law; Huldah says judgment will still come. He renews the covenant and keeps a great Passover, but dies at Megiddo fighting Pharaoh Necho, and Jeremiah laments him.

title: The Fall of Judah and Cyrus's Decree
summary: Judah's last kings, Jehoahaz, Jehoiakim, Jehoiachin and Zedekiah, rule briefly under Egyptian and Babylonian power, and the people scorn God's messengers until there is no remedy. Nebuchadnezzar burns the temple, breaks down Jerusalem's walls and carries the people to Babylon, and the land lies desolate until it has kept its Sabbaths for seventy years, as Jeremiah had said. In Cyrus's first year the LORD stirs him to proclaim that the temple be rebuilt and that any of God's people may go up.
